e: Control Tower data residency guardrails, or SCPs in AWS Organizations, can deny access to all Regions except ap-northeast-3 and prevent internet access for VPCs, enforcing the rules centrally across accounts. WAF doesn't control VPC internet gateways, per-user IAM or NACL rules are not centrally enforceable, and AWS Config only detects and alerts.

EventBridge scheduled rules can invoke Lambda functions to start and stop the RDS instance on a schedule, so the database isn't running (and billed for compute) outside the 12-hour window. Session Manager, ElastiCache, or an EC2 cron host don't provide a simple, cheap start/stop mechanism.

A lifecycle policy moving objects from S3 Standard to Standard-IA after 90 days keeps recent files readily available and cuts cost for older ones, with no monitoring fees for millions of objects. Standard-IA as the initial tier charges retrieval fees for new popular files, and S3 inventory only reports on objects, it doesn't move them.

S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a 365-day retention period prevents anyone, including privileged users, from modifying or deleting files for 1 year. Governance mode can be overridden by authorized users, a legal hold has no fixed duration, and IAM or Lambda hash tracking can't truly enforce immutability.

CloudFront caches content from S3 at edge locations worldwide, so users get fast, reliable access regardless of location, and access to confidential files can be restricted using origin access control. DataSync, Global Accelerator, and SQS aren't content caching solutions for S3.

Lake Formation blueprints with Glue crawl and ingest batch and streamed data into S3 in Parquet, a low-overhead data lake. Athena then runs one-time queries directly on S3 and QuickSight builds KPI dashboards. Custom Lambda to Redshift, OpenSearch clusters, or Kinesis Data Analytics for ad hoc queries add overhead.

Automated backups of Aurora are limited to 35 days, so AWS Backup is used to keep backups for 5 years and then delete them automatically. Exporting database audit logs to CloudWatch Logs keeps them indefinitely (no expiration). Manual snapshots don't expire on their own.

CloudFront delivers both live streaming and video on demand through its global edge network, caching and accelerating content for a worldwide audience. Global Accelerator isn't a content cache, Route 53 is DNS, and S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads rather than viewer streaming.

An AWS WAF rule (for example, rate limits, bot control, or IP rules) filters malicious requests before they reach the API, and a usage plan with API keys limits access to genuine users. Handling IPs inside Lambda wastes invocations, a private API breaks public access, and per-user IAM roles don't scale.
At only 300 MB a month with 30-day retention and millisecond access, S3 Standard is cheapest and simplest. Glacier doesn't give millisecond access, and OpenSearch or RDS cost much more for backups.

S3 events triggering Lambda scale automatically for thousands of runs a day, with high availability and no servers to manage, and results go to Aurora. EC2, EBS Multi-Attach, or ECS on EC2 all need infrastructure management.

FSx for Lustre is a high-performance file system for HPC on Linux and integrates with S3: it can load data from S3 and write results back to S3 for long-term persistence. FSx for Windows is for Windows workloads, and Glacier or EBS don't provide a shared high-performance file system for hundreds of instances.

ECR stores the images, and ECS on Fargate runs containers without managing servers, with target tracking auto scaling and high availability. The EC2 launch type or self-managed EC2 hosts keep the operational overhead the company wants to avoid.

SQS decouples the two applications, holds messages for up to days, and a dead-letter queue keeps failed messages so they don't block the rest. Redis on EC2 means management, Kinesis is for streaming, and SNS doesn't retain messages for slow consumers.

Enable AWS WAF on the CloudFront distribution so all requests are inspected, and use an OAI (or OAC) so the S3 bucket is reachable only through CloudFront and can't be accessed directly, bypassing WAF. S3 bucket policies can't use a WAF ARN, and security groups don't apply to S3.

CloudFront with the S3 bucket as origin caches static pages at edge locations worldwide, handling millions of views efficiently and cheaply. Presigned URLs, replicating to every Region, or Route 53 geoproximity don't provide global caching.

Reserved Instances cover the steady baseline at a discount, and On-Demand Instances add capacity reliably when traffic rises, so processing continues without downtime. Spot Instances can be interrupted, and RI-only for peak capacity wastes money during intermittent traffic.

A service control policy attached at the root OU applies to all accounts in the organization and lets the security team maintain permission guardrails in one place. ACLs, security groups, and per-account cross-account roles are not scalable or central.

AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection for ALBs, including detection, mitigation, and cost protection. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, Macie classifies sensitive data, and GuardDuty only detects threats.
AWS WAF on the ALB supports geographic match rules, so you can allow requests only from a specific country. Security groups and network ACLs work with IP address ranges and can't filter by country.

API Gateway with Lambda is serverless and scales automatically and elastically with seasonal spikes, with no capacity planning. EC2-based options need scaling configuration and don't scale as quickly.

CloudFront field-level encryption encrypts specific sensitive fields at the edge with a public key, so only applications holding the private key can decrypt them, protecting data throughout the stack. Signed URLs and cookies control access to content, and HTTPS alone protects only data in transit.

CloudFront caches the same videos and images at edge locations worldwide, reducing load on S3 and cost, and speeding delivery to millions of users. Global Accelerator and ElastiCache don't cache static S3 content cost-effectively for global viewers.

Spreading the Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones (three instances each) with the ALB makes the architecture highly available without changing the application. Multi-Region designs need application changes and more complexity, and round-robin doesn't add AZ resilience.

RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, reducing connection overhead on Aurora and preventing timeouts from Lambda's many open connections, with only a change to the endpoint in the function. The other options don't address connection exhaustion or require major changes.
